{"body":"Implements ADR-063 (#2039) — **as amended by this issue onto #2187's vocabulary.** Part of #1819.

> **Rewritten 2026-09-28.** The original text was built on `disposition: exhausted` → `escalate`. #2187 (closed 2026-09-25) retired both: `exhausted` hid *which* budget ran out and mapped to a response nothing implemented. The words are now `timed_out` and `out_of_turns`, both → **retry** (`core/pipeline/disposition.sh`), and "did not finish" is the predicate `disposition_unfinished`. Most of the original scope has also landed during the [Phase 0/F] migrations. What follows is what is actually left. The remaining §1 budget blocks and the `exhausted` wording sweep were split to #2222 on 2026-09-28.

**Build Mode: Dogfood** — ADR-057 gate 4. The run executes the installed engine from `main`, not this branch: A and B change `core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh` and plugin code, none of it in the hot-reloaded contract-reader closure (`_runner_contract_lib_closure`, all `scripts/lib`), and no template or roster change — so the run building this is not graded by it (gate 2 does not fire). A convergence defect would surface in later runs, behind CI and the human merge gate, not stop the next run before intake (gate 3 does not fire).

**Blocked on:** #1835 (`plan`) and #1838 (`impact`) — the last two model-driven stages still on `result_contract` v1. Not on #1850 (Phase 1) and not on the rest of [Phase 0/F].

## Where each ADR-063 section stands today

| ADR-063 | as written | now | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| §1 budget reaches the prompt from the enforcing value | one shared helper | per-stage `_<stage>_budget_guidance`, each reading `_route_resolve_timeout` / `_route_resolve_max_turns` — design, monitor, plan, review-lens, review-report, test-author, spec-correspondence | **done for 7**; missing on `impact` (hand-written "BUDGET DISCIPLINE" prose, `plugins/agent/impact/plugin.sh:218`), `security-lens`, `spec-coverage`, `issue-acceptance` → #2222 |
| §2 each stage declares a partial form | — | `design` keeps a design written before a timeout (#2186, `plugins/agent/design/plugin.sh:615`); `plan`/`impact` already have partial shapes | done where it matters |
| §3 partial signalled as `exhausted` | new emitters | **one classifier**: `router_reason_disposition` (`scripts/lib/router-rc-classify.sh:259`) maps `router_timeout`→`timed_out`, `router_out_of_turns`→`out_of_turns`. Used by design, monitor, review-lens, security-lens, test-author, issue-acceptance, build | **done for 7**; `plan`/`impact` arrive with #1835/#1838; `spec-coverage`, `spec-correspondence`, `review-report` hardcode `disposition: "complete"` |
| §4 gates fail closed on partial | `exhausted → escalate` + gate rule | the escalate half is gone (retry is the response; budget growth on retry is `_route_escalate_timeout` inside the router, `core/router/route.sh:872`). **The gate rule was never built** | **open — this is the work** |

## The defect that is live today (§4)

ADR-063 warned that letting a stage hand back partial work before §4 exists "swaps a loud failure for a quiet one". #2186 shipped the first half without the second:

1. `design` times out after writing `design.md` → it **keeps** the file, writes `verdict: incomplete, disposition: timed_out`, and says "spec-coverage and design-gate judge whether it is complete" (`plugins/agent/design/plugin.sh:604-622`).
2. `design-gate` never reads design's disposition; it checks structure and always writes `disposition: complete` (`plugins/tool/design-gate/plugin.sh:228`).
3. `design_verify_cycle.exit_when` reads only `design-gate.verdict == pass` and `spec-coverage.verdict != uncovered` (`config/templates/simple.yaml:117-120`).
4. The cycle's "an unfinished member cannot converge" rule (#1208, `core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh:2608`) applies **only to the commit member** (`_cycle_commit_member` → `capabilities.produces_commits`). `design` produces no commits, so it is exempt.

→ A truncated design whose structure is valid converges the cycle and goes to build.

A second path to the same place: `spec-coverage` calls `route_to_model … || true`; a timeout yields no parseable reply → `verdict: unreadable, disposition: complete` (`plugins/agent/spec-coverage/plugin.sh:~175`). `unreadable` satisfies `!= uncovered`, so **a spec-coverage timeout also lets the cycle exit**, and the cause (`timed_out`) is dropped.

*(Both found by reading the code on 2026-09-28. The red tests below are what prove them.)*

## Scope

**A. §4 — an unfinished member cannot converge its cycle (engine).**
Generalise the #1208 suppression from "the commit member" to **any member of the iteration** whose disposition satisfies `disposition_unfinished`. The iteration then re-runs (or, at `max_iterations`, takes the existing exhaustion path, which already reads `_iter_did_not_finish`). No per-stage names: keyed on the disposition word alone, as #1208 is.

**B. §3 — the gates that call a model name why they stopped.**
`spec-coverage`, `spec-correspondence` and `review-report`: route the router's terminated reason through `router_reason_disposition` instead of hardcoding `complete`. A reply that never came is `timed_out`/`out_of_turns`/…, not `complete` + `unreadable`. With A in place, a timed-out `spec-coverage` can no longer read as "not uncovered".

**C. ADR-063 amendment.**
Status → Accepted, amended: §3 uses `timed_out`/`out_of_turns` via `router_reason_disposition`; §4's escalate half is struck (retry + router-side timeout growth replace it); §1 records that the invariant is *"rendered from the enforcing value"*, satisfied by per-stage helpers — not "one helper". Dated back-pointer to #2187.

## Out of scope

- The remaining §1 budget blocks (`impact`, `security-lens`, `spec-coverage`, `issue-acceptance`) and retiring the live `exhausted` wording — split to #2222 (Dogfood) on 2026-09-28.
- `plan` and `impact` emitting §3 dispositions — #1835 / #1838.
- Budget *growth* on retry — already in the router (ADR-029).
- #1850 (drop the v1 reader) — Phase 1, after #1798.

## Acceptance

Write each red first; state in the PR body the assertion and how it failed.

- [ ] **A, red first:** a `design_verify_cycle` fixture where `design` returns `disposition: timed_out` with a structurally valid `design.md`, `design-gate` passes and `spec-coverage` is `covered` → the cycle does **not** converge on that iteration. Red at the merge-base (it converges today).
- [ ] **A:** the same fixture with `disposition: complete` still converges (the suppression is keyed on the word, not the stage).
- [ ] **A:** at `max_iterations` with the last iteration unfinished, the cycle takes the existing exhaustion path — not `complete`.
- [ ] **B, red first:** `spec-coverage` with a router that times out → `disposition: timed_out`, and `design_verify_cycle` does not exit on it. Same shape for `spec-correspondence` and a `review-report` lens.
- [ ] **C:** ADR-063 amended and accepted; no section still prescribes `exhausted` or `escalate`.
- [ ] `npm test` and `npm run lint` green.

Refs ADR-063, ADR-054 §6/§6a, ADR-057, #2187, #2186, #1208, #1261, #1819.

Filed into **Initiative 1.3 / Phase 0**, and **blocked on [Phase 0/F]** — #1833–#1850, all 18 still open.

Not a preference. `disposition` is a **v2-only field**. `runner_read_stage_disposition` (`core/pipeline/verdict.sh:674`) reads `_d_disp` from the result file, and `_verdict_read_result` resolves `result_contract // 1`; ADR-054 §6 states the vocabulary is consulted only at `result_contract >= 2`.

**None of the eight LLM stages is on v2 today.** Verified:

| stage | result_contract |
|---|---|
| `plan`, `impact`, `build`, `design`, `monitor`, `review-lens`, `security-lens`, `review-report` | v1 (undeclared) |

So a stage emitting `disposition: exhausted` before its [Phase 0/F] migration would write a field nothing reads — an inert mechanism, indistinguishable from a working one. That is the exact defect this repo keeps paying for: #2024's kill loop, #1976 "computed, written, and discarded", #1977 "the mechanism was inert". Landing this early would manufacture another instance of it.

### Sits naturally in [Phase 0/G]

#1832 (G) moved `did_not_finish`, `empty_diff`, `scope_too_large` and `inert_build` **into** disposition. This is the other half: making stages actually *emit* one of the words that already has an engine response.

`exhausted` is already wired — `disposition.sh:53` (in the set), `:97` (`→ escalate`), `dispatch-rc.sh:177` (`rc=10 →`), `route.sh:749` (`_route_escalate_timeout`, +50% capped at 2×, ADR-029). Nothing produces it.

### One half is NOT blocked

ADR-063 §1 — telling the model its turn budget and timeout from the enforcing value — needs no v2. It is prompt text, and `plan`/`impact`/`build` already do it. Five stages do not: `design`, `monitor`, `review-lens`, `security-lens`, `review-report`.

That half could land independently and is where the #1833 run's cost actually was — nine design calls that each began from nothing. Worth splitting out if the F migration is a long road.

### Order when it comes up

1. [Phase 0/F] migrations complete (#1850 drops the v1 read path)
2. shared budget block, from `_route_resolve_router_timeout` / `_route_resolve_max_turns` — never a hand-copied number
3. each stage declares a partial form of its deliverable
4. `disposition: exhausted` on the way out
5. **gates fail closed on `exhausted`** — the half that makes the rest safe; without it a half-built design passes silently","createdAt":"2026-09-02T07:40:58Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/ezigus/zBuild/issues/2032#issuecomment-5506190547","viewerDidAuthor":false},{"id":"IC_kwDOSmjmcc8AAAABYJwrKA","author":{"login":"github-actions"},"authorAssociation":"CONTRIBUTOR","body":"<!-- zbuild-run-status run_id=20260930165521-2271 -->
